options.name: modbus-auth
options.setting-help: the auth scheme the cache's own Modbus clients must speak: suite (the crypt handshake) or none

value-help.suite: every client proves the shared auth-key with the suite handshake right after connect — the cache answers OK, or ERR and the client is dropped

options.help: the auth scheme the cache's own Modbus clients must speak: `suite` demands the crypt handshake (magic + nonce + HMAC proof of the shared key) right after every connect and drops the client on ERR/anything else; none/empty = no auth at all

options.name: modbus-auth-key
options.setting-help: the suite handshake's shared key for the cache's clients, min 16 characters (`file:<path>` reads an owner-only file)
options.help: the shared key the cache's clients prove with the suite handshake (min 16 characters); the value may be `file:<path>` — the first line of an owner-only 0600 file (a systemd LoadCredential rides as file:/run/credentials/...)

options.name: modbus-auth-upstream
options.setting-help: the auth scheme the cache speaks to the upstream inverter: suite (the crypt handshake), waveshare (the gateway connection password) or none

value-help.suite: after every connect, prove the shared auth-upstream-key with the suite handshake — the inverter answers OK, or ERR and the connection fails
value-help.waveshare: after every connect, send the shared auth-upstream-key as the Waveshare TCP connection password — the gateway answers OK, or anything else/nothing and the connection fails

options.help: the auth scheme toward the upstream inverter: `suite` proves the shared auth-upstream-key with a crypt handshake right after every connect (the peer answers OK, or ERR and the connection fails — the poller keeps retrying); `waveshare` sends the shared auth-upstream-key as the Waveshare TCP connection password right after every connect (the gateway answers OK, or anything else/nothing and the connection fails — the poller keeps retrying); none/empty = no auth at all

options.name: modbus-auth-upstream-key
options.setting-help: the key the cache presents upstream: the suite handshake's shared key (min 16 characters) or the Waveshare gateway password (`file:<path>` reads an owner-only file)
options.help: the key the cache presents to the upstream inverter — the suite handshake's shared key (min 16 characters) or the Waveshare TCP connection password (non-empty ASCII, the gateway's own rule); the value may be `file:<path>` — the first line of an owner-only 0600 file (a systemd LoadCredential rides as file:/run/credentials/...)

options.help: seconds between cache polls

options.help: seconds between consecutive inverter reads within a poll cycle, 0 = no delay

options.help: max register gap when merging ranges into block reads, 0 = read ranges separately

options.help: per-register cache TTL: cached registers older than this are refetched from the inverter, 0 = never expire, serve last known values forever

options.name: allow-write
options.setting-help: forward write requests (FC05/06/15/16/22/23) to the device

value-help.on: forward writes (the ACLs and the allow-list still gate them)
value-help.off: refuse writes with a Modbus illegal-function exception (the default)

options.help: forward write requests (FC05/06/15/16/22/23) to the inverter; without it they refuse with a Modbus illegal-function exception

options.name: write-registers
options.setting-help: the address ranges a write may touch (FC06/16/22/23 registers, FC05/15 coils): START:COUNT,... or the device profile's acl

value-help.profile: the device profile's write acl (acl/write: the rule chain, default deny any)

options.help: address ranges a (forwarded) write may touch — the register writes (FC06/16/22/23) and the coil writes (FC05/15, the coil space) are gated by the same ranges: comma-separated START:COUNT, e.g. 47400:100,47600:100; "any" = unrestricted; "none" = nothing writable; "profile" = the device profile's write acl ("acl": {"write": {"rules": [{"type": "allow"|"deny", "range": "START:COUNT"}]}} — a whitelist: the last matching rule decides, a register no rule decides refuses); "file:<path>" = the standalone acl file (the same gate object a profile carries under "acl"/"write", read and compiled at start and on every set)

options.name: modbus-profile
options.setting-help: device profile JSON: the register ranges to cache (a bare name resolves in profiles/profiles/)
options.help: device profile JSON (the shared profiles/ schema)

options.name: selection
options.setting-help: selection JSON: which profile names to fetch ("all" = every entry, "none" = cache nothing)

value-help.none: cache nothing: the map empties, every read forwards, nothing is stored

options.help: selection JSON: {"registers": ["pv-power",...]} — the profile names to fetch

options.name: connect-acl
options.setting-help: clients allowed to connect: "any", "none", comma-separated IPs/prefixes, or file:<path> (the ip-prefix acl file)

value-help.none: no client may connect: every connection is rejected

options.help: clients allowed to connect: "any", "none" (refuse everyone), comma-separated IPs/prefixes like 10.0.0.7,10.48.0.0/16, or "file:<path>" — the standalone ip-prefix acl file (the gate object {"type": "ip-prefix", "rules": [{"type": "allow"|"deny", "prefix": ...}]}: the last matching rule decides, a client no rule decides refuses; "any" = 0.0.0.0/0, the whole space)

options.name: write-acl
options.setting-help: clients allowed to write (requires allow-write): "any", "none", comma-separated IPs/prefixes, or file:<path> (the ip-prefix acl file)

value-help.any: the write gate is allow-write alone

options.help: clients allowed to write (requires --allow-write): "any", "none" (refuse everyone), comma-separated IPs/prefixes, or "file:<path>" — the standalone ip-prefix acl file (the same gate object acl/connect reads: the last matching rule decides, a client no rule decides refuses)

options.help: a second, read-only control token: sessions authenticating with it may run its policy's verbs only (the default policy: show,flush) (no set/clear, no request poll now, no request dump/restore, no restart, no shutdown) — the ops shift against the admin key, both audited; the value may be `file:<path>` — the first line of an owner-only 0600 file (a systemd LoadCredential rides as file:/run/credentials/...)

options.name: dump-path
options.setting-help: the state dump file: written behind, on request dump and every dump-interval
options.help: the state dump (write-behind): the live setting overrides and — with --dump-with-cache — the cached words, as one JSON, written 0600 with an integrity hash (a restore refuses a tampered, unsigned or group-writable dump); dumped on shutdown, on the request dump command and every --dump-interval seconds; loaded on start only with --restore-on-start, on demand with the request restore command

options.name: dump-key
options.setting-help: the key that seals the state dumps (the words and the settings, the reload's state file too) (`file:<path>` reads an owner-only file)
options.help: the key that seals the state dumps and the reload's state file: the words and the settings ride encrypted (an HMAC-SHA256 counter-mode keystream, authenticated — a restore refuses a wrong or missing key, and a configured key refuses an unsealed dump); the reload re-exec re-resolves the same key, so the state file reads on the other side; no key = the dumps stay 0600 plaintext with the integrity hash; a dump path without a key warns at start and on set; the value may be `file:<path>` — the first line of an owner-only 0600 file (a systemd LoadCredential rides as file:/run/credentials/...)

options.name: dump-with-cache
options.setting-help: the dump carries the cached register words too
options.help: dump the cached words too: `request dump` and the --dump-interval loop write the words + the settings (`request dump with-cache` always includes them; the restore takes either shape) ($DUMP_WITH_CACHE)

options.name: dump-interval

options.name: restore-on-start
options.help: load the state dump when the daemon starts (needs --dump-path) — a restart serves last-known values instead of cold misses; without it the dump loads on demand ($RESTORE_ON_START)
